comments.body:
## RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1 — confirmed at runtime)

**Mechanism.** pytest's default `prepend` import mode inserts a collected module's *basedir*
(its first ancestor without `__init__.py`) at `sys.path[0]`. `tests/unit/` has no
`__init__.py`, so collecting ANY `tests/unit/**` module puts `tests/unit` at `sys.path[0]`.
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/__init__.py` (empty, 0 bytes) then makes that directory an
importable top-level package named `rebar_reconciler`, **shadowing** the engine package that
`tests/scripts/conftest.py:28-30` puts on `sys.path` further down.

`tests/scripts/reducer/test_managed_refs.py:42-48` exec's `outbound_differ.py` standalone via
`spec_from_file_location` with no package context, so its module-level
`from rebar_reconciler._loader import lazy_load` (`outbound_differ.py:31`) resolves
`rebar_reconciler` through ordinary top-level machinery — and gets the empty test-dir package,
which has no `_loader` submodule.

The repo already has a compensating mechanism for exactly this shadow:
`_seed_dotted_namespace()` in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/conftest.py:51-79` appends the engine
`rebar_reconciler` directory to the shadow package's `__path__` so "ANY engine submodule falls
through generically" (its own comment). It was added by f32b19b1e7.

**The defect is that the compensation is installed one directory too deep.** It lives in
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/conftest.py`, so it fires only when `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/**`
is collected — but the shadow it compensates for is created by ANY `tests/unit/**` collection.

**Discriminating evidence.** I instrumented the failing fixture to print
`rebar_reconciler.__file__` / `__path__` / `sys.path[:6]` at the moment `outbound_differ` is
exec'd. Three runs, one varying input (which `tests/unit` modules are in the selection):

| selection | `rebar_reconciler.__file__` | `__path__` | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| the reducer test alone | `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__init__.py` | `[engine pkg]` | PASS |
| `+ tests/unit/test_epoch_guard_matrix.py` | `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/__init__.py` | `['tests/unit/rebar_reconciler']` | **ERROR (reported)** |
| `+ tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_lock_steal.py` | `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/__init__.py` | `['tests/unit/rebar_reconciler', 'src/.../rebar_reconciler']` | PASS |

In the failing run `sys.path[0]` was `tests/unit` with the engine dir at index 3. Row 3 is the
decisive one: the shadow is *present and harmless* once the `__path__` extension has run, which
rules out the rival explanations — it is not a `sys.path` ordering race per se, not a stale
`__pycache__`, not a `sys.modules` pin (no seeded key was involved), and not an installed
site-packages copy (none exists in the venv).

**Why the full suite is green.** Conftests import at *collection* time for the whole arg set, so
a run that includes `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/**` always fires the compensation. The bug is
reachable only when `tests/unit/**` is collected WITHOUT `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/**` — which
pytest-randomly's varying selections and any developer's partial selection produce.

**The compensation is already duplicated, which corroborates the scoping defect.** Two further
copies exist, both in `tests/unit/` top level, each with a comment pointing back at the conftest:
`tests/unit/test_canonical_consolidation.py:59-71` and
`tests/unit/test_code_review_artifact.py:110-118`. Two prior authors hit this same shadow from a
top-level `tests/unit` module and patched locally rather than hoisting.

**Legitimacy: `defect`.** An existing test errors, and the behaviour violates the cited design
invariant of `_seed_dotted_namespace()` itself — that engine submodules resolve generically under
the shadow.

**Repair is mechanical (verified, not asserted).** An independent adversarial pass measured the
alternatives and eliminated them on evidence, leaving one: hoist the `__path__` extension to
`tests/unit/conftest.py`.
- deleting `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/__init__.py` -> 10 collection errors (23 files there use
  relative imports), plus 8 sub-packages would become generically-named top-level packages;
- `--import-mode=importlib` -> 9512 collected / 23 errors vs. a clean 11198 / 0 baseline;
- renaming the directory -> 290 tracked files, 53 references across 30 files, and it discards the
  deliberate `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/` mirroring;
- changing the engine -> bends production code (194 dotted imports across 54 modules) to a test
  directory's name.

**One trap recorded for the implementer:** placing the hoist *after*
`tests/unit/conftest.py:21-22` is WRONG. By then the engine dir is `sys.path[0]`, so
`import rebar_reconciler` permanently binds the ENGINE package before pytest creates the shadow;
`__path__.append` becomes a no-op and `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` then dies with
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rebar_reconciler.conftest'`. It looks green on the
ticket's repro and is red one command over. The extension must resolve the shadow while
`tests/unit` is still `sys.path[0]` (or seed it explicitly).

**Guard shape.** An in-process assertion would be masked in CI — a full-suite run always collects
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/**`, so the invariant holds even with the fix reverted (measured: the
naive guard passes when run alongside `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_lock_steal.py`). The guard
must therefore be a subprocess, matching the precedent already in
`tests/unit/test_engine_dir.py::test_library_path_exposes_no_generic_top_level_engine_names`,
whose docstring cites the same masking hazard.

compiled_state.description:
Running any `tests/unit/*` module in the same pytest session as `tests/scripts/reducer` makes `tests/scripts/reducer/test_managed_refs.py::test_unlink_after_compaction_still_propagates_removal` error with:

    ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rebar_reconciler._loader'
    (raised from src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py:31)

Reproduced deterministically on PRISTINE origin/main (53b9c3e6dd), so this is pre-existing and not caused by the change that surfaced it (e63c):

    # 413 passed, 1 skipped -- clean
    pytest tests/interfaces/queries tests/scripts/reducer tests/scripts/graph -q -p no:randomly

    # 417 passed, 1 skipped, 1 ERROR -- adding ANY tests/unit module triggers it
    pytest tests/interfaces/queries tests/unit/<any> tests/scripts/reducer tests/scripts/graph -q -p no:randomly

The test passes in isolation (10 passed). `tests/scripts/` relies on `src/rebar/_engine` being on sys.path so `rebar_reconciler` imports as a top-level package; something in the tests/unit conftest/import path removes or shadows that, and the submodule import then fails.

Why it matters: pytest-randomly is enabled, so suite ordering varies per run. A developer running a mixed selection sees a failure that is not theirs, which is exactly the false signal that makes people distrust and then ignore the suite. It also means a real regression in that test could be masked or misattributed.

Not scoped to a fix here -- filed so it is not rediscovered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The mixed selection above passes
- [ ] The sys.path/import contract for `tests/scripts/` is made explicit rather than ambient
- [ ] A guard prevents silent reintroduction (e.g. the suite asserts the import contract holds)
